description:
FILED s481b (2026-09-10, Opus) while measuring the critical-infrastructure
milestone (#1607).  Found from Mojolicious, whose `Mojo::File` cannot load.

REPRODUCER (scratch/s481b/probe-filecopy.pl), perl 5.40.3 vs ./runpcl:

    require File::Copy;
    print "loaded\n";
    print "copy=", (File::Copy::copy("/etc/hostname", "/tmp/hc") ? 1 : 0), "\n";

    perl: loaded / copy=1
    PCL : PCL: statement not supported at
          /â¦/lib/5.40.3/File/Copy.pm line 238: ) --
          Handle single node of unknown type. Dump: â¦

THE DROPS, five of them, all in `sub cp` (line 208).  `pl2cl --module` exits 0
and prints nothing, because `--module` silences the #339 announcement; with
`PCL_DROP_ANNOUNCE=all` they appear:

    line 238: )   -- Handle single node of unknown type
    line 239: }   -- "
    line 241: }   -- "
    line 242: }   -- "
    line 246: }   -- "

Bare `)` and `}` as whole "statements" is the signature of a LEXING CASCADE:
one token is misread and the rest of the block falls out of the structure.  The
trigger is line 238,

    236:     my $ok = $fromstat[5] == $tostat[5];   # group must match
    237:     if ($ok) {                             # and we must be in group
    238:         $ok = grep { $_ == $fromstat[5] } split /\s+/, $)

â the magic variable `$)` at the end of a statement with NO trailing
semicolon, as the last argument of `split`, inside a `grep BLOCK LIST` inside
two nested `if`s.

WHAT DOES **NOT** REPRODUCE (recorded so it is not re-derived): the statement
in isolation is fine.  `my @g = split /\s+/, $);` and
`my $x = grep { $_ == $g[0] } split /\s+/, $);` both agree with perl, and so
does a hand-written copy of lines 230-243 with the same nesting and the same
missing semicolon (scratch/s481b/probe-dollar-paren.pl,
probe-dollar-paren2.pl).  So the mis-lex depends on the DOCUMENT, not on the
statement â read it as a PPI-state cascade and bisect on the real file's own
sub, not on a reconstruction.  If PPI turns out to tokenize it wrongly, the
finding belongs in `docs/ppi-upstream-bugs.md` + `docs/ppi-bug-report.t`
(CLAUDE.md rule 13).

TWO SECOND-ORDER POINTS WORTH KEEPING:

  * **`pl2cl --module` exits 0 on a file it cannot fully compile.**  The
    refusal only speaks at RUN time, in the middle of somebody's `require`.
    That is the same silence #1472 measured for child processes.
  * **This drop is in no census population.**  `baselines/parse-error-drop-
    census-s399.tsv` covers the sweep, the board, `Pl/t`, perl's own `t/`,
    `cpan-tests/` and PCL's `lib/` â not the CORE modules PCL loads from the
    system perl at run time.  File::Copy is one of those, and there may be
    more; a seventh population (the core modules a corpus run actually loads,
    which `PCL_DROP_LOG` can already collect) would count them.
subject: CORE `File::Copy` CANNOT BE LOADED: `require File::Copy` dies "PCL: statement not supported at File/Copy.pm line 238", and the transpile SILENTLY drops five statements there (`--module` mode suppresses the announcement).  It blocks Mojo::File and anything that copies a file.  The drop is in no census population, because core modules loaded at run time are counted nowhere.
